questions.stem: A 70-year-old man comes to the office because of a 2-month history of increasingly severe back pain. He rates the pain as 8 on a 10-point scale. Use of acetaminophen and naproxen has provided no relief. He underwent total prostatectomy for prostate cancer 1 year ago. He appears healthy. He is 185 cm (6 ft 1 in) tall and weighs 80 kg (176 lb); BMI is 23 kg/m². Temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse is 80/min, respirations are 17/min, and blood pressure is 147/77 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no other abnormalities. Serum studies are most likely to show increased activity or concentration of which of the following?
questions.stemHtml: A 70-year-old man comes to the office because of a 2-month history of increasingly severe back pain. He rates the pain as 8 on a 10-point scale. Use of acetaminophen and naproxen has provided no relief. He underwent total prostatectomy for prostate cancer 1 year ago. He appears healthy. He is 185 cm (6 ft 1 in) tall and weighs 80 kg (176 lb); BMI is 23 kg/m². Temperature is 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse is 80/min, respirations are 17/min, and blood pressure is 147/77 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no other abnormalities. Serum studies are most likely to show increased activity or concentration of which of the following?
questions.subject: Hematology/Oncology

explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: Prostate cancer is known to cause metastatic disease, with

a high rate of metastasis to the bones, likely causing this patient’s back pain. When bone metastasis is present, serum studies are most likely to show an increased alkaline phosphatase concentration.

Evaluation: This patient has a known history of prostate cancer, a common cancer in men.

Pain is the most likely presenting symptom of bone metastasis in prostate cancer.

Definition: The bone lesions identified in metastatic prostate cancer are usually

osteoblastic rather than osteolytic. The most common laboratory findings in cases of bone metastatic prostate cancer include increased prostate-specific antigen, increased serum alkaline phosphatase, and decreased hemoglobin.

Prevention: The risk for metastatic prostate cancer may be prevented with screening;

however, shared decision-making should be used. Early detection of prostate cancer has not necessarily been found to correlate with improved clinical outcomes.

Treatment: Prostate cancer may be treated with surveillance, radiation therapy, and/or

radical prostatectomy. In higher risk prostate cancer or metastatic disease, androgen

deprivation therapy and chemotherapy may be indicated.

Differential: This patient with a history of prostate cancer presents with severe low back

pain and mildly increased temperature without abnormalities identified on physical examination, which makes bone prostate metastatic disease a likely cause of his pain. Alkaline phosphatase is the most likely to show an increased concentration on serum studies, as metastatic prostate disease often presents with osteoblastic lesions.

wrongAnswers.B: Calcium is incorrect. Increased calcium would be more likely in cases of osteolytic lesions. Metastatic prostate cancer is more likely to present with osteoblastic disease rather than osteolytic disease.
wrongAnswers.C: 1,25-Dihydroxyvitamin D is not the most likely to be increased on serum studies. 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, also known as calcitriol, is the active form of 25- hydroxyvitamin D. 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D may be increased in cases of sarcoidosis.
wrongAnswers.D: Parathyroid hormone is incorrect. Parathyroid hormone is a peptide hormone that increases osteoclast activity, vitamin D synthesis, and renal calcium reabsorption to maintain calcium homeostasis. Alkaline phosphatase is the most likely to be increased on serum studies in cases of bone metastatic prostate cancer.
wrongAnswers.E: Parathyroid hormone-related peptide is not the most likely to be increased on serum studies. Lung cancer is often complicated by hypercalcemia caused by paraneoplastic parathyroid hormone-related peptide production. This phenomenon occurs in the setting of squamous cell lung cancer and may also occur in squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, as well as breast and renal cancers.

explanationPanel.rule: Prostate cancer bone metastases are typically osteoblastic, so back pain with prior prostate cancer points to increased alkaline phosphatase.
explanationPanel.trap: Do not pick calcium/PTHrP unless the stem is describing osteolytic hypercalcemia or a PTHrP paraneoplastic syndrome.

layer4.trap: Do not pick calcium/PTHrP unless the stem is describing osteolytic hypercalcemia or a PTHrP paraneoplastic syndrome.

questions.stem: A 1-day-old male newborn is evaluated in the newborn nursery in the hospital after pulse oximetry on room air showed an oxygen saturation of 89%. He was delivered in the hospital at 35 weeks’ gestation to a 30-year-old primigravid woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Length was 50 cm (19.6 in) and weight was 3714 g (8 lb 3 oz) at delivery. Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. Physical examination shows tachypnea, systolic murmur, and cyanosis. Today, cardiac examination shows no S₂ splitting. Subsequent two-dimensional echocardiography shows transposition of the great arteries and an intact atrial septum. Operative intervention with atrial septostomy is planned. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this patient at this time?

questions.subject: Cardiology

explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: This patient, with a congenital cyanotic heart disease,

requires maintained patency of the ductus arteriosus to permit blood oxygenation. Patency can be maintained after birth with intravenous alprostadil, the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this patient, pending surgical correction.

Evaluation: Cyanosis, hypoxia, and a cardiac murmur at birth suggest the presence of a

congenital cyanotic heart disease, confirmed by echocardiography. Suspicion of significant cyanotic heart disease should prompt treatment with prostaglandins, such as alprostadil (a synthetic prostaglandin E1 analog), to maintain the patency of the ductus arteriosus and prevent cardiopulmonary arrest.

Definition: In utero, oxygenated blood is obtained from the placenta, not from the lungs,

and the ductus arteriosus allows the shunting of oxygenated blood from the pulmonary artery directly to the aorta while bypassing the fetal lungs, which are filled with amniotic fluid. In cases of cyanotic heart disease, where a lesion in the heart prevents pulmonary oxygenation after birth by shunting blood around the lungs, maintaining the patency of the ductus arteriosus permits some admixture of oxygenated blood for tissue delivery.

Prevention: Cases of known or suspected cyanotic heart disease should be evaluated via

fetal echocardiography prior to birth. As many cases are genetic in origin, there is no specific preventive measure apart from prenatal genetic counseling.

Treatment: Immediate treatment with intravenous alprostadil is indicated in suspected

cases of cyanotic heart disease, while planning definitive operative repair.

Differential: Alprostadil is indicated for maintaining the patency of the ductus arteriosus in

congenital cyanotic heart disease. Medications such as corticosteroids, ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs, and β-adrenergic blockers do not play a role in maintenance of a patent ductus arteriosus, and in some cases (eg, indomethacin), would result in undesired closure of the physiologic shunt.

wrongAnswers.B: Betamethasone is incorrect. Betamethasone is used prior to delivery to promote fetal lung maturity and surfactant production. It does not have a role in maintaining the patency of the ductus arteriosus.
wrongAnswers.C: Captopril is not the best choice and it is no longer a preferred first-line treatment. Captopril was often used in the management of pediatric heart failure, but such management would occur after surgical management of a cyanotic lesion and maintenance of patency of the ductus arteriosus.
wrongAnswers.D: Indomethacin is incorrect. Indomethacin inhibits prostaglandin E1 production, which promotes closure of the ductus arteriosus and would be potentially fatal in this patient’s case.
wrongAnswers.E: Labetalol is incorrect. Labetalol is a mixed α- and β-adrenergic blocker used in hypertension and heart failure, among other uses. It does not have a role in the maintenance of a patent ductus arteriosus.

explanationPanel.rule: Cyanotic ductal-dependent congenital heart disease requires alprostadil to keep the PDA open until definitive repair.
explanationPanel.trap: Indomethacin closes the ductus arteriosus and can be fatal in ductal-dependent lesions.

layer4.rule: Cyanotic ductal-dependent congenital heart disease requires alprostadil to keep the PDA open until definitive repair.
layer4.trap: Indomethacin closes the ductus arteriosus and can be fatal in ductal-dependent lesions.

questions.stem: An 18-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his parents 2 hours after they discovered that he had been sleeping with a knife under his pillow. When his parents asked him about it, the patient told them that "the Mafia" has been following him for the past 6 weeks and has threatened to kill him. He says he can hear members of the Mafia making threatening comments even when he is in his bedroom alone. He insists that he will use the knife to protect himself if needed. He has no history of serious medical or psychiatric illness and takes no medications. His maternal grandparents both had bipolar disorder. The patient binge drinks alcoholic beverages once weekly. He says he tried cannabis once 6 months ago. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination discloses no abnormalities. On mental status examination, he describes his mood as "anxious" and has a blunted and guarded affect. He has no current suicidal or homicidal ideation. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy?

questions.subject: Psychiatry

explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: This patient is demonstrating symptoms consistent with a

first presentation of schizophrenia, including delusions and a flat affect. Atypical antipsychotics, such as aripiprazole, are considered to be first-line treatments for schizophrenia.

Evaluation: Patients with schizophrenia demonstrate at least two of the following five

symptoms: delusions (eg, persecutory delusions about the Mafia), hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized behavior, or negative symptoms (eg, flat affect, apathy, alogia). Negative symptoms may also manifest as poor personal hygiene. Many patients also experience prodromal periods of strange behavior and decreased functioning. The total duration of symptoms must exceed 6 months to meet diagnostic criteria. However, it is important to recognize the characteristic symptoms of a first presentation of schizophrenia (as in this patient) as treatment should not be delayed for 6 months while awaiting a formal diagnosis.

Definition: The cause of schizophrenia is thought to include dopamine dysregulation, and

brain imaging typically shows decreased cortical volume and enlarged ventricles. A family history of bipolar disorder or schizophrenia is common.

Prevention: Though there is no universal way to prevent schizophrenia, avoiding cannabis

use during adolescence (especially in patients with a family history of serious mental illness) is likely beneficial for decreasing future schizophrenia risk.

Treatment: Treatment of schizophrenia requires antipsychotics, which can be divided into

two groups: typical (haloperidol, fluphenazine, chlorpromazine) and atypical (risperidone, aripiprazole, olanzapine).

Differential: Typical antipsychotics are effective, though because they potently antagonize

dopamine receptors, they are associated with movement disorders such as acute dystonia, parkinsonism, akathisia, and tardive dyskinesia. As atypical antipsychotics carry a decreased movement disorder risk, they are commonly considered to be first-line treatments.

wrongAnswers.B: Buspirone is incorrect. Buspirone is a serotonin modulator used to treat generalized anxiety disorder. It is not useful in schizophrenia treatment.
wrongAnswers.C: Haloperidol is incorrect. Haloperidol is a typical antipsychotic that can be used in schizophrenia spectrum disorders. However, it potently antagonizes dopamine receptors and is associated with movement disorders such as acute dystonia, parkinsonism, akathisia, and tardive dyskinesia. As atypical antipsychotics carry a decreased movement disorder risk, they are commonly recommended as first-line schizophrenia treatments.
wrongAnswers.D: Sertraline is incorrect. Sertraline, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, is used in the treatment of depression, generalized anxiety disorder, and obsessive-compulsive disorder. Sertraline is not useful in schizophrenia treatment.
wrongAnswers.E: Valproic acid is incorrect. Valproic acid is an anticonvulsant and mood stabilizer used in bipolar disorder and schizoaffective disorder. As it addresses mood but not psychotic symptoms, it is not useful in schizophrenia treatment.

explanationPanel.rule: First-episode psychosis with delusions, hallucinations, and negative symptoms is treated with an atypical antipsychotic.
explanationPanel.trap: Do not wait for 6 months of symptoms before treating, and avoid haloperidol when an atypical option is available due to EPS risk.

layer4.rule: First-episode psychosis with delusions, hallucinations, and negative symptoms is treated with an atypical antipsychotic.
layer4.trap: Do not wait for 6 months of symptoms before treating, and avoid haloperidol when an atypical option is available due to EPS risk.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman comes to the office because of a 6-week history of upper abdominal discomfort and swelling. Six weeks ago, she underwent cholecystectomy because of severe gallstone pancreatitis that resolved slowly. She takes no medications. She is 168 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and weighs 66 kg (146 lb); BMI is 24 kg/m². Vital signs are within normal limits. Cardiopulmonary examination discloses no abnormalities. Abdominal examination shows a subtly palpable, 6-cm, mildly tender mass in the midepigastric region. CT scan of the abdomen is shown; the arrow indicates an abnormality. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

She is 168 cm (5 ft 6 in) tall and weighs 66 kg (146 lb); BMI is 24 kg/m². Vital signs are within normal limits. Cardiopulmonary examination discloses no abnormalities. Abdominal examination shows a subtly palpable, 6-cm, mildly tender mass in the midepigastric region. CT scan of the abdomen is shown; the arrow indicates an abnormality. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.subject: Gastroenterology

explanationPanel.correct: C. Endoscopic drainage of the lesion
explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: This patient with a recent history of gallstone pancreatitis

presents with abdominal pain after cholecystectomy and is found to have a lesion on CT scan of the abdomen most consistent with a pancreatic pseudocyst. The most appropriate next step in management is endoscopic drainage of the lesion.

Evaluation: Pancreatic pseudocysts are fluid-filled cavities that arise as complications

from pancreatitis or pancreatic duct obstruction. During an episode of pancreatitis, enzymes may leak into the surrounding tissues and lead to inflammatory tissue formation and encapsulation of the fluid. Patients often present with abdominal pain and a palpable mass in the epigastric region.

Definition: CT scan of the abdomen is the gold standard for diagnosis of these lesions.

Further evaluation may be conducted with endoscopic ultrasonography and fine-needle aspiration, which would help distinguish pancreatic pseudocysts from other lesions.

Prevention: The mainstay of prevention for pancreatic pseudocyst formation involves

mitigating risk factors for pancreatitis such as alcohol use and proper gallstone treatment.

Treatment: Most pancreatic pseudocysts resolve spontaneously and do not require

treatment. If pancreatic pseudocysts are causing complications (eg, infection) or symptoms are severe, such as in this patient, endoscopic drainage of the lesion may be performed.

Differential: The differential includes other cystic lesions such as neoplastic lesions. In this

patient with a recent history of pancreatitis and confirmatory imaging findings, the most likely diagnosis is a pancreatic pseudocyst.

wrongAnswers.A: CT-guided percutaneous aspiration is incorrect. This would be difficult to achieve in this patient due to the anatomic location of the pseudocyst. Endoscopic drainage of the lesion is the preferred approach.
wrongAnswers.B: Distal pancreatectomy is incorrect. Pancreatic pseudocysts are benign and heal with time. A distal pancreatectomy would be unnecessary in this setting and is typically reserved for patients with distal pancreatic neoplasms.
wrongAnswers.D: Open laparotomy and excision is incorrect. Open laparotomy and excision of the pancreatic pseudocyst would place this patient at risk for complications from unnecessary surgery.
wrongAnswers.E: Observation is not the most appropriate next step. Since this patient is having severe symptoms, she would benefit from endoscopic drainage.

explanationPanel.rule: A symptomatic pancreatic pseudocyst several weeks after pancreatitis is managed with endoscopic drainage.
explanationPanel.trap: Observation is for asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic pseudocysts, not a painful palpable 6-cm lesion.

layer4.rule: A symptomatic pancreatic pseudocyst several weeks after pancreatitis is managed with endoscopic drainage.
layer4.trap: Observation is for asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic pseudocysts, not a painful palpable 6-cm lesion.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman comes to the office because she is concerned about her risk for developing Alzheimer disease. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. Her father had moderate dementia, Alzheimer type, and died at the age of 88 years of viral pneumonia. Her paternal aunt had severe dementia, Alzheimer type, and died at the age of 80 years. The patient drinks two to three glasses of wine weekly. She works as a successful writer. She is not married, has no close family, and worries that there will be no one to take care of her if she develops dementia. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Cognitive testing shows no evidence of impairment. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.stemHtml: A 55-year-old woman comes to the office because she is concerned about her risk for developing Alzheimer disease. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. Her father had moderate dementia, Alzheimer type, and died at the age of 88 years of viral pneumonia. Her paternal aunt had severe dementia, Alzheimer type, and died at the age of 80 years. The patient drinks two to three glasses of wine weekly. She works as a successful writer. She is not married, has no close family, and worries that there will be no one to take care of her if she develops dementia. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Cognitive testing shows no evidence of impairment. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.subject: Neurology

explanationPanel.correct: E. Recommendation for regular aerobic exercise
explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: Regular aerobic exercise plays a major role in the

prevention of dementia, Alzheimer type (AD), and would likely improve this patient’s future outcomes if recommended.

Evaluation: AD is the most prevalent dementia in older patients. It classically presents

with progressive cognitive decline that begins with short-term memory impairment, progresses to apraxia and language abnormalities, and culminates in behavioral and personality changes preventing the patient from performing basic activities of daily living.

Definition: AD is postulated to result from decreased cholinergic signaling in the cortex

and basal forebrain.

Prevention: AD prevention involves dietary changes (including maximizing produce, fish,

nuts, and olive oil and limiting saturated fat and sugar), regular physical exercise, mentally stimulating activities (eg, puzzles), management of cardiovascular risk factors such as diabetes mellitus and hypertension, stress reduction, and smoking cessation. Aerobic exercise can decrease cardiovascular risk factors, promote neurogenesis by increasing exercise-induced metabolic factors such as ketones, and decrease inflammation.

Treatment: Treatment commonly consists of cholinesterase inhibitors (eg, donepezil).

Differential: Genetic testing is not routinely recommended in asymptomatic individuals with

a family history of late-onset AD, as the results may not be definitive due to incomplete penetrance but may be useful in patients with a family history of early-onset AD (onset of AD in individuals younger than 65 years).

wrongAnswers.A: Donepezil therapy is incorrect. Donepezil is a cholinesterase treatment used in AD treatment. It is not useful for AD prevention.
wrongAnswers.B: Genetic testing is incorrect. Genetic testing is not routinely recommended in asymptomatic individuals with a family history of late-onset AD but may be useful in patients with a family history of AD that occurs at age 65 or younger.
wrongAnswers.C: MRI of the brain is incorrect. Though some patients may show early signs of AD on neuroimaging, these findings are nonspecific and neuroimaging is not routinely used for this purpose.
wrongAnswers.D: Neuropsychological testing is incorrect. Neuropsychological testing can help clarify a dementia diagnosis in unclear cases. However, the routine use of neuropsychological testing before a patient is symptomatic is not recommended as it is resource intensive and not particularly sensitive to early cognitive changes in AD.

explanationPanel.rule: Asymptomatic late-onset Alzheimer family history is managed with risk-reduction counseling such as regular aerobic exercise.
explanationPanel.trap: Genetic testing is not routine for asymptomatic late-onset Alzheimer disease; it is mainly considered for early-onset familial patterns.

layer4.rule: Asymptomatic late-onset Alzheimer family history is managed with risk-reduction counseling such as regular aerobic exercise.
layer4.trap: Genetic testing is not routine for asymptomatic late-onset Alzheimer disease; it is mainly considered for early-onset familial patterns.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman is admitted to the hospital because of increasingly severe abdominal pain, bloating, nausea, and persistent emesis. She has recurrent high-grade serous ovarian cancer that has been resistant to several rounds of chemotherapy. Current management is decompression by nasogastric tube and bowel rest. Today, she is accompanied by her son, who is her primary caretaker. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis shows extensive abdominal carcinomatosis, hepatic and pleural masses, and a partial bowel obstruction. The physician meets with the patient and her son and explains that further surgical management or other cancer therapies are not indicated, and that her life expectancy is less than 6 months. Before out-of-hospital placement can be arranged, the patient sustains a myocardial infarction and requires mechanical ventilation. While in the ICU, she has a stroke and is not expected to recover. In accordance to her wishes, her son decides to allow palliative extubation. He then asks about organ donation. The patient's electronic health record indicates that she is an organ donor. Which of the following organs is most likely suitable for donation?

questions.subject: Ethics/Social Sciences

explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: Unlike other solid organs, corneal transplants are generally

considered safe in cases of metastatic cancer such as this one.

Key Concept: Organ donation is generally contraindicated in patients with metastatic

cancer because of the increased risk for cancer transmission in solid organs. However, there are a few notable exceptions, including the cornea. Explanation: The cornea is an avascular tissue, decreasing the chance of cancer cell dissemination to the cornea. Caution should still be exercised, but corneal transplants are generally considered safe in cases of metastatic cancer.

Differential: Solid organs can be considered for donation in patients without metastatic

disease depending on several factors, including donor demographics and comorbidities, organ-specific structural abnormalities, and other factors.

wrongAnswers.B: Heart, kidney, liver, and lung are incorrect. Transplantation of any of these organs may result in cancer transmission. As well, this patient’s heart, liver, and lungs have been involved in her disease and may have structural or functional contraindications to transplantation.
wrongAnswers.C: Heart, kidney, liver, and lung are incorrect. Transplantation of any of these organs may result in cancer transmission. As well, this patient’s heart, liver, and lungs have been involved in her disease and may have structural or functional contraindications to transplantation.
wrongAnswers.D: Heart, kidney, liver, and lung are incorrect. Transplantation of any of these organs may result in cancer transmission. As well, this patient’s heart, liver, and lungs have been involved in her disease and may have structural or functional contraindications to transplantation.
wrongAnswers.E: Heart, kidney, liver, and lung are incorrect. Transplantation of any of these organs may result in cancer transmission. As well, this patient’s heart, liver, and lungs have been involved in her disease and may have structural or functional contraindications to transplantation.

explanationPanel.rule: Metastatic cancer generally excludes solid-organ donation, but avascular corneas are usually acceptable.
explanationPanel.trap: Do not choose heart, liver, lung, or kidney because solid organs can transmit malignancy and may be involved by disease.

questions.subject: Pulmonology

explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: This patient’s dyspnea, dry cough, bilateral basilar crackles,

and a restrictive pattern on pulmonary function testing (PFT) are consistent with pulmonary fibrosis, most likely secondary to bleomycin therapy.

Key Concept: Pulmonary fibrosis can be a consequence of multiple medications, including

bleomycin, methotrexate, and amiodarone. Explanation: Pulmonary fibrosis is a chronic, progressive lung disease characterized by scarring of the lung parenchyma. It typically presents with shortness of breath, especially with physical activity, dry cough, fatigue, and weight loss. PFTs will show a normal or increased FEV₁:FVC ratio, decreased total lung capacity, and decreased diffusion capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide. While it may be idiopathic, pulmonary fibrosis can result from medication use, occupational exposures, and autoimmune disorders.

Differential: All medications, especially chemotherapeutic agents, have a variety of side

effects that can limit their use. Of this patient’s medications, however, bleomycin is the

most likely cause of his pulmonary fibrosis.

wrongAnswers.B: Dacarbazine is incorrect. Dacarbazine is an antineoplastic agent used in the treatment of multiple cancers. The most common side effects include nausea and vomiting, as well as bone marrow suppression. While anemia could cause dyspnea, this patient has normal cell counts.
wrongAnswers.C: Doxorubicin is incorrect. Doxorubicin is a chemotherapeutic agent with cardiotoxic effects. Specifically, doxorubicin leads to myocyte damage that results in dilated cardiomyopathy. While congestive heart failure associated with cardiomyopathy could result in worsening dyspnea, it would likely be associated with symptoms such as weight gain, persistent lower extremity edema, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, which are not seen in this patient.
wrongAnswers.D: Vinblastine is incorrect. The most common toxicity associated with vinblastine use is bone marrow suppression. Less commonly, acute dyspnea can follow the administration of vinblastine, but this would not result in persistent symptoms with restrictive disease on PFT.

explanationPanel.rule: Bleomycin causes pulmonary fibrosis with dyspnea, crackles, restrictive PFTs, and decreased DLCO.
explanationPanel.trap: Doxorubicin is the anthracycline cardiomyopathy drug, not the classic restrictive lung fibrosis drug.

questions.stem: A 16-month-old boy is admitted to the hospital for treatment of a rectal abscess that developed 4 days ago. He underwent incision and drainage of the abscess in the clinic 2 days ago, but the area of redness and induration on his right buttock has persisted. Oral cephalexin therapy was initiated 2 days ago, but he continues to be febrile with temperatures to 38.9°C (102.0°F). He has also lost approximately 0.5 kg (1 lb) during the past 6 weeks. Application of warm compresses to the affected area has not provided improvement. Medical history is remarkable for a left perianal fistula that was surgically removed 6 weeks ago and rectal abscesses 2 and 6 months ago, which were treated with incision and drainage. He receives no additional medications and has no known drug allergies. He eats some solid foods and drinks 22 oz of whole cow milk daily. Vaccinations are up-to-date. He is 75 cm (2 ft 6 in; 2nd percentile) long and weighs 9.2 kg (20 lb; 12th percentile); head circumference is 46 cm (18 in; 25th percentile). Temperature is 38.6°C (101.5°F), pulse is 150/min, respirations are 22/min, and blood pressure is 90/64 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 97%. The patient appears fussy and uncomfortable. Physical examination discloses a 3 × 3-cm area of induration and erythema on the right buttock that is draining pus. The remainder of the physical examination discloses no abnormalities. Current culture results show methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus. Which of the following studies is most likely to establish the underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?

choices: Antibody titers to previously administered vaccines
questions.subject: Infectious Disease

explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: This patient who presents with nonhealing and recurrent

pyogenic abscesses infected with methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus most likely has chronic granulomatous disease. A neutrophil oxidative burst test is most likely to confirm the diagnosis.

Evaluation: Chronic granulomatous disease is caused by NADPH oxidase deficiency and

results in impaired intracellular killing of pathogens, particularly catalase-positive organisms. It classically presents as recurrent pyogenic infections with catalase-positive organisms such as S. aureus.

Definition: Chronic granulomatous disease occurs when there is a defect in the production

of reactive oxygen species, such as superoxide and hydrogen peroxide. This results in a nonfunctional respiratory burst in neutrophils, increasing a patient’s susceptibility to catalase-positive pathogens. Chronic granulomatous disease is diagnosed with a dihydrorhodamine test or nitroblue tetrazolium reduction test. The dihydrorhodamine test, also referred to as the neutrophil oxidative burst test, measures the ability of the respiratory burst in neutrophils. A defect within the respiratory burst is consistent with chronic granulomatous disease.

Prevention: Prevention of infection in these patients includes prophylactic antibiotics and

antifungals.

Treatment: Early diagnosis and treatment of infection is crucial in patients with chronic

granulomatous disease.

Differential: This patient with disseminated infection may have a variety of

immunodeficiencies; however, his recurrent pyogenic abscesses with S. aureus are most consistent with chronic granulomatous disease, which is diagnosed with a neutrophil oxidative burst test.

wrongAnswers.A: Antibody titers to previously administered vaccines, lymphocyte subset panel, and serum immunoglobulin concentrations are incorrect. The patient’s B lymphocytes and humoral response to infection is intact, but the deficit is within the intracellular killing of pathogens.
wrongAnswers.B: Antibody titers to previously administered vaccines, lymphocyte subset panel, and serum immunoglobulin concentrations are incorrect. The patient’s B lymphocytes and humoral response to infection is intact, but the deficit is within the intracellular killing of pathogens.
wrongAnswers.D: Serum hemolytic complement (CH50) assay is incorrect. The CH50 assay is abnormal in patients with classical pathway complement deficiencies. This pathway would remain intact in patients with chronic granulomatous disease, the most likely diagnosis in this case.
wrongAnswers.E: Antibody titers to previously administered vaccines, lymphocyte subset panel, and serum immunoglobulin concentrations are incorrect. The patient’s B lymphocytes and humoral response to infection is intact, but the deficit is within the intracellular killing of pathogens.

explanationPanel.rule: Recurrent pyogenic S aureus abscesses suggest chronic granulomatous disease, confirmed by neutrophil oxidative burst testing.
explanationPanel.trap: Normal vaccine titers or immunoglobulin testing addresses humoral immunity, not defective intracellular killing.

layer4.rule: Recurrent pyogenic S aureus abscesses suggest chronic granulomatous disease, confirmed by neutrophil oxidative burst testing.
layer4.trap: Normal vaccine titers or immunoglobulin testing addresses humoral immunity, not defective intracellular killing.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man comes to the office because of a 2-day history of a clear, odorless discharge from his penis. He has not had pain with urination. He has no history of serious illness. He does not take any medications or use any substances. He had sexual intercourse with a new partner 10 days ago; he did not use condoms. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no lymphadenopathy, edema, genital lesions, or obvious penile discharge. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.stemHtml: A 20-year-old man comes to the office because of a 2-day history of a clear, odorless discharge from his penis. He has not had pain with urination. He has no history of serious illness. He does not take any medications or use any substances. He had sexual intercourse with a new partner 10 days ago; he did not use condoms. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows no lymphadenopathy, edema, genital lesions, or obvious penile discharge. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
choices: Microscopic examination of the penile discharge
questions.subject: Infectious Disease

explanationPanel.correct: E. Urine nucleic acid amplification test
explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: Chlamydia trachomatis, which is the most likely cause of

this patient’s symptoms, can cause sexually transmitted urethritis. The diagnosis can be confirmed with a urine nucleic acid amplification test, which is the most appropriate next step in management for this patient.

Evaluation: Urethritis typically presents with watery urethral discharge as well as dysuria,

although patients are frequently asymptomatic.

Definition: Urethritis in men is commonly due to sexually transmitted infection (STI) by C.

trachomatis and/or Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Risk factors for STIs include adolescence, multiple sexual partners, and not using barrier contraception, such as condoms. Prompt identification and treatment of STIs can prevent spread to or reinfection of sexual partners and decrease the risk for complications, such as pelvic inflammatory disease (in women) and sterility.

Prevention: STIs may be prevented by using barrier contraception, such as condoms.

Treatment: Combination therapy with intramuscular ceftriaxone and oral azithromycin is

the most used regimen to provide adequate coverage against N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis.

Differential: This patient presents with painless clear and odorless discharge from his

penis after recent sexual intercourse with a new partner where condoms were not used. Infection with C. trachomatis is the most likely cause of his symptoms. The diagnosis can be confirmed with a urine nucleic acid amplification test.

wrongAnswers.A: Doxycycline therapy is not the most appropriate next step in management. Doxycycline is a common medication used in the treatment of C. trachomatis infection. However, diagnosis with a urine nucleic acid amplification test would be the most appropriate next step in management. Doxycycline also requires a prolonged course of therapy, which may limit adherence.
wrongAnswers.B: Microscopic examination of the penile discharge is incorrect. Urine nucleic acid amplification testing is the preferred diagnostic technique to identify infection with C. trachomatis. Microscopic examination in cases of epididymitis or prostatitis secondary to C. trachomatis may identify an increased number of leukocytes.
wrongAnswers.C: Serum antibody test is not the correct answer. Serum antibody testing may be used to identify cases of STIs, such as syphilis or hepatitis B. Urine nucleic acid amplification testing is more appropriate in this case of painless urethral discharge.
wrongAnswers.D: Urethral swab culture is not the most appropriate next step in management. The patient in this case is presenting with painless urethral discharge, which is likely secondary to infection with C. trachomatis. Urine nucleic acid amplification testing is more accurate than swab culture.

explanationPanel.rule: Urethritis after unprotected sex is evaluated with urine NAAT for Chlamydia and gonorrhea.
explanationPanel.trap: Do not rely on urethral culture or microscopy when NAAT is the preferred diagnostic test.

layer4.rule: Urethritis after unprotected sex is evaluated with urine NAAT for Chlamydia and gonorrhea.
layer4.trap: Do not rely on urethral culture or microscopy when NAAT is the preferred diagnostic test.

questions.stem: A 13-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was found unconscious in the desert by hikers. It is estimated that he was lost in the desert for 36 hours without adequate water intake. He has no history of serious illness and receives no medications. Height is at the 50th percentile, weight is at the 50th percentile, and BMI is at the 64th percentile. Temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F), pulse is 138/min, respirations are 26/min, and blood pressure is 90/62 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 98%. On arrival, he is awake but confused. Physical examination shows decreased skin turgor and dry mucous membranes. Serum sodium concentration is 160 mEq/L. Intravenous administration of which of the following is most appropriate for this patient?
questions.stemHtml: A 13-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was found unconscious in the desert by hikers. It is estimated that he was lost in the desert for 36 hours without adequate water intake. He has no history of serious illness and receives no medications. Height is at the 50th percentile, weight is at the 50th percentile, and BMI is at the 64th percentile. Temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F), pulse is 138/min, respirations are 26/min, and blood pressure is 90/62 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 98%. On arrival, he is awake but confused. Physical examination shows decreased skin turgor and dry mucous membranes. Serum sodium concentration is 160 mEq/L. Intravenous administration of which of the following is most appropriate for this patient?
questions.subject: Nephrology/Urology

explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: This patient is dehydrated as a result of prolonged

inadequate free water intake. Dehydration can lead to a variety of electrolyte disturbances, including hypernatremia. Treatment is with correction of volume depletion. Intravenous isotonic crystalloid infusion with 0.9% saline (which contains 154 mEq/L of sodium) is the most appropriate treatment for this patient, as this will correct volume depletion while causing minimal risk for overly rapid correction of hypernatremia.

Key Concept: Inadequate free water intake leads to dehydration and to a variety of

electrolyte disturbances including hypernatremia, defined as a serum sodium concentration greater than 145 mEq/L. Explanation: Under normal conditions, increases in serum osmolarity are detected by the hypothalamus, resulting in increased secretion of vasopressin and in increased thirst, resulting in renal retention of free water and in increased water intake, respectively. Patients typically present with altered mental status and clinical evidence of volume depletion (such as tachycardia, hypotension, orthostasis, poor skin turgor, and dry mucous membranes). Treatment is with correction of volume depletion. Isotonic crystalloid infusion with 0.9% saline (which contains 154 mEq/L of sodium) is preferable, as this will correct volume depletion while causing minimal risk for overly rapid correction of

hypernatremia. The rate of correction is dependent on the suspected duration of hypernatremia. Acute hypernatremia of less than 24 hours' duration can be corrected rapidly, but more chronic hypernatremia should be corrected more slowly (at a maximum rate of approximately 6 to 9 mEq/day) to avoid cerebral edema.

Differential: Of the options listed, 0.9% saline is the only isotonic solution and is therefore

the most appropriate choice for safe fluid resuscitation of this patient.

wrongAnswers.A: 0.2% and 0.45% saline are incorrect. While these hypotonic solutions can correct volume depletion, infusion of hypotonic solution increases the risk for overly rapid sodium correction, which may lead to cerebral edema.
wrongAnswers.B: 0.2% and 0.45% saline are incorrect. While these hypotonic solutions can correct volume depletion, infusion of hypotonic solution increases the risk for overly rapid sodium correction, which may lead to cerebral edema.
wrongAnswers.D: 3% saline is incorrect. Apart from its use in nonelectrolyte-related cerebral herniation syndromes, hypertonic saline is reserved for patients with severe, acutely symptomatic hyponatremia, not hypernatremia. Administration of 3% saline will worsen his hypernatremia.

explanationPanel.rule: Severe volume depletion with hypernatremia is initially resuscitated with isotonic 0.9% saline.
explanationPanel.trap: Hypotonic fluids can correct sodium too rapidly and precipitate cerebral edema.

layer4.rule: Severe volume depletion with hypernatremia is initially resuscitated with isotonic 0.9% saline.
layer4.trap: Hypotonic fluids can correct sodium too rapidly and precipitate cerebral edema.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 34 weeks' gestation is admitted to the hospital 45 minutes after the sudden onset of vaginal bleeding and increasingly frequent episodes of abdominal pain, which has been increasing in severity. She has not had loss of vaginal fluid. She has received routine prenatal care. She has hypertension treated with labetalol. Her only other medication is a prenatal vitamin. Her previous pregnancy was uncomplicated and ended in spontaneous vaginal delivery of a healthy newborn at term. The patient appears uncomfortable. Temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 110/min and regular, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 150/85 mm Hg. Abdominal examination discloses diffuse tenderness to palpation. On pelvic examination, the uterus is consistent in size with a 30-week gestation. Fetal heart tracing is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

She has not had loss of vaginal fluid. She has received routine prenatal care. She has hypertension treated with labetalol. Her only other medication is a prenatal vitamin. Her previous pregnancy was uncomplicated and ended in spontaneous vaginal delivery of a healthy newborn at term. The patient appears uncomfortable. Temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 110/min and regular, respirations are 16/min, and blood pressure is 150/85 mm Hg. Abdominal examination discloses diffuse tenderness to palpation. On pelvic examination, the uterus is consistent in size with a 30-week gestation. Fetal heart tracing is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
questions.subject: Obstetrics

explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: Abruptio placentae should be expected in this patient with

third-trimester vaginal bleeding, severe abdominal pain, and fetal distress as evidenced by recurrent late decelerations on fetal heart monitoring. The most appropriate next step in management is immediate cesarean delivery.

Evaluation: Abruptio placentae classically presents in the third trimester with vaginal

bleeding, severe abdominal or pelvic pain, and tetanic contractions. Fetal distress is typically present.

Definition: Abruptio placentae, or placental abruption, is a premature separation of the

placenta from the uterine endometrium. The uterus is typically exquisitely tender to palpation and may present with a clinical picture like peritonitis with pain out of proportion to examination findings and abdominal rigidity. Due to the compromised fetal blood supply,

placental abruption is an obstetric emergency.

Prevention: Risk factors include preeclampsia, cocaine use, trauma, and smoking, so

prevention is aimed at minimizing or avoiding these disorders and exposures.

Treatment: Treatment of placental abruption includes an emergent cesarean delivery.

Differential: Hydralazine and magnesium sulfate therapy may be used in the treatment of

preeclampsia, but this patient does not currently meet criteria for its diagnosis. Oxytocin is classically used to induce labor, but this patient is already having frequent uterine contractions. A biophysical profile can be used to assess fetal health, but this patient’s fetal heart monitoring with recurrent late decelerations suggests a fetus in distress.

wrongAnswers.A: Biophysical profile is incorrect. A biophysical profile is a screening test that uses a nonstress test and ultrasonographic evaluation to determine fetal well-being. A biophysical profile measures fetal heart rate, breathing, movement, and tone, as well as the amniotic fluid volume. It is done prenatally for at-risk pregnancies, not in a patient with an obstetric emergency in active labor.
wrongAnswers.B: Hydralazine therapy is incorrect. Hydralazine is used in the treatment of hypertension, both pre-existing and related to preeclampsia, during pregnancy. This patient’s mild hypertension is likely related to pain, and decreasing her blood pressure may compromise fetal blood flow, making this answer choice incorrect.
wrongAnswers.D: Magnesium sulfate therapy is incorrect. Magnesium sulfate therapy is the mainstay of treatment in preeclampsia, which classically presents with hypertension, proteinuria, and end-organ dysfunction after the 20th week of gestation. This patient does not meet diagnostic criteria for preeclampsia currently and has clear indications for an immediate cesarean delivery.
wrongAnswers.E: Oxytocin therapy is incorrect. Oxytocin is standardly used to induce labor and after delivery to prevent postpartum hemorrhage. This patient is having active uterine contractions in the setting of placental abruption and should be taken to the operating room for immediate cesarean delivery.

explanationPanel.rule: Third-trimester bleeding plus abdominal pain/tender uterus and recurrent late decelerations requires immediate cesarean delivery.
explanationPanel.trap: Do not delay for a biophysical profile or treat mild hypertension when the fetus is already in distress.

layer4.rule: Third-trimester bleeding plus abdominal pain/tender uterus and recurrent late decelerations requires immediate cesarean delivery.
layer4.trap: Do not delay for a biophysical profile or treat mild hypertension when the fetus is already in distress.

questions.stem: A hospitalized 66-year-old man is being evaluated for discharge 2 days after undergoing an uncomplicated left femoral popliteal bypass operation. He has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His medications are lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. He drinks one glass of wine twice weekly. He appears well. He is 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and weighs 95 kg (210 lb); BMI is 35 kg/m². His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 72/min, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 120/78 mm Hg. Examination shows a clean, dry surgical incision over the left lower extremity. Which of the following factors in this patient’s history most strongly indicates an increased risk for disease recurrence?
questions.stemHtml: A hospitalized 66-year-old man is being evaluated for discharge 2 days after undergoing an uncomplicated left femoral popliteal bypass operation. He has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. His medications are lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. He drinks one glass of wine twice weekly. He appears well. He is 178 cm (5 ft 10 in) tall and weighs 95 kg (210 lb); BMI is 35 kg/m². His temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 72/min, respirations are 12/min, and blood pressure is 120/78 mm Hg. Examination shows a clean, dry surgical incision over the left lower extremity. Which of the following factors in this patient’s history most strongly indicates an increased risk for disease recurrence?
questions.subject: Cardiology

explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: There are multiple risk factors for peripheral artery disease

(PAD), with tobacco use being one of the strongest. Estimates suggest a four times higher relative risk for PAD in smokers than nonsmokers, making this patient’s tobacco use the factor in his history that most strongly indicates an increased risk for recurrence.

Key Concept: Risk factors for PAD include smoking, age, obesity, hypertension,

hyperlipidemia, diabetes mellitus, family history, and chronic kidney disease, among others. Explanation: PAD refers to blocked arteries in the limbs, though atherosclerotic disease may affect any vascular bed. Patients with PAD may report limb claudication, or pain felt in the affected limb during exertion. Physical examination may disclose sarcopenia, waxy and hairless skin, diminished pulses, and discoloration of the skin of the affected extremity. In severe cases, or in cases of acute arterial occlusion, bypass surgery to salvage the limb may be indicated. This patient is now recovering from femoral popliteal bypass to manage PAD. In terms of recovery, smoking cessation is critical, as tobacco use is a strong risk factor for disease recurrence.

Differential: While managing hypertension is also important, smoking carries the greatest

risk for disease recurrence, especially since this patient’s blood pressure is managed with lisinopril.

wrongAnswers.A: Alcohol use is incorrect. Alcohol is not known to be a strong risk factor for the development of PAD.
wrongAnswers.B: Aspirin therapy is incorrect. Aspirin use is not a known risk factor for the development of PAD and may be protective because aspirin limits platelet aggregation and decreases the risk for atherosclerotic plaque rupture leading to arterial occlusion.
wrongAnswers.C: Hypertension and lisinopril therapy do not most strongly indicate an increased risk for disease recurrence. While hypertension is a risk factor for PAD, this patient’s blood pressure is well controlled on lisinopril, diminishing its potential to promote disease progression.
wrongAnswers.D: Hypertension and lisinopril therapy do not most strongly indicate an increased risk for disease recurrence. While hypertension is a risk factor for PAD, this patient’s blood pressure is well controlled on lisinopril, diminishing its potential to promote disease progression.
wrongAnswers.E: Obesity does not most strongly indicate an increased risk for disease recurrence. Obesity, as a component of metabolic syndrome, is known to be a risk factor for PAD; however, it is not as significant of a risk factor as tobacco use.

explanationPanel.rule: Smoking is the strongest listed risk factor for recurrent peripheral artery disease after bypass.
explanationPanel.trap: Controlled hypertension and obesity matter, but tobacco use is the dominant modifiable recurrence risk.

layer4.rule: Smoking is the strongest listed risk factor for recurrent peripheral artery disease after bypass.
layer4.trap: Controlled hypertension and obesity matter, but tobacco use is the dominant modifiable recurrence risk.

questions.stem: Investigators conduct a randomized study of the efficacy of a new medication compared with lisinopril for the treatment of hypertension. The investigators recruit 200 patients aged 30 to 75 years with hypertension. Patients are randomly assigned to receive either the new medication (100 patients) or lisinopril (100 patients) and are observed for 1 year. Patients come to the study clinic biweekly to undergo measurement of blood pressure. After 1 year, 40 patients who received the new medication and 60 patients who received lisinopril are still taking the assigned medication. All study participants undergo biweekly measurement of blood pressure until the completion of the study. Which of the following is the most appropriate method to use for data analysis?
questions.stemHtml: Investigators conduct a randomized study of the efficacy of a new medication compared with lisinopril for the treatment of hypertension. The investigators recruit 200 patients aged 30 to 75 years with hypertension. Patients are randomly assigned to receive either the new medication (100 patients) or lisinopril (100 patients) and are observed for 1 year. Patients come to the study clinic biweekly to undergo measurement of blood pressure. After 1 year, 40 patients who received the new medication and 60 patients who received lisinopril are still taking the assigned medication. All study participants undergo biweekly measurement of blood pressure until the completion of the study. Which of the following is the most appropriate method to use for data analysis?
choices: Analyze the results available for patients who took the assigned medication for the duration of the study
End the study now and do not analyze the data
Include data up until the time of discontinuation for patients who discontinued study medication
Recruit additional patients to both study arms and extend the study for 6 additional months
questions.subject: Biostatistics/Epidemiology

explanationPanel.correct: C. Include data for all patients
explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: Including data for all patients is the most appropriate

method to use for data analysis in clinical trials. This is called intention-to-treat analysis.

Key Concept: Intention-to-treat analysis is used to compare groups in clinical trials based

on initial group assignments. Intention-to-treat analysis avoids potential biases associated with study group attrition, participant crossover, and participant noncompliance that may impact the results of the study. Explanation: Clinical trials are designed to allow for an adequate number of participants to be recruited so that the study may achieve sufficient power to properly evaluate a clinical outcome. These trials are designed to account for participant attrition during the trial period. In this study, participants from both groups are lost to follow-up. Intention-to-treat analysis avoids biases that are associated with partial data sets, which may show skewed results.

Differential: In studies analyzing the effectiveness of a new treatment, randomization

distributes patients more evenly and minimizes risk for bias. Most clinical trials suffer attrition, which is accounted for in the determination of sample size. Despite participant attrition, intention-to-treat analysis is recommended to avoid biases that may be associated with analysis of a partial data set.

wrongAnswers.A: Analyze the results available for patients who took the assigned medication for the duration of the study is incorrect. Analyzing these results would evaluate a partial data set of patients. Due to attrition in the study, there may be biases associated with the remaining participants, which could ultimately impact study outcomes.
wrongAnswers.B: End the study now and do not analyze the data is incorrect. Intention-to-treat analysis is used for clinical trials to avoid potential biases that may affect study outcomes. Although there was participant attrition in the trial, all patients should be analyzed in the final data analysis.
wrongAnswers.D: Include data up until the time of discontinuation for patients who discontinued study medication is incorrect. Analyzing these results would evaluate a partial data set of patients. Due to attrition in the study, there may be biases associated with remaining participants, which could ultimately impact study outcomes.
wrongAnswers.E: Recruit additional patients to both study arms and extend the study for 6 additional months is incorrect. Prior to study initiation, power calculations are used to determine an adequate sample size. Recruiting additional patients to the study arms may skew the outcomes of the study.

explanationPanel.rule: Randomized trials with attrition should analyze all participants in their originally assigned groups by intention-to-treat.
explanationPanel.trap: Per-protocol or partial-data analysis reintroduces attrition/nonadherence bias.

layer4.rule: Randomized trials with attrition should analyze all participants in their originally assigned groups by intention-to-treat.
layer4.trap: Per-protocol or partial-data analysis reintroduces attrition/nonadherence bias.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman comes to the office because of a 3-month history of a tingling sensation in the ring and small fingers of her left hand. The sensation initially occurred immediately upon awakening each morning and lasted for several minutes. Two months ago, the tingling sensation became more severe and began to awaken her during the night. She also had the onset of similar symptoms in her left arm and elbow during this time. The sensation now occurs throughout the day. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. Vital signs are within normal limits. Muscle strength is 4/5 on abduction and adduction of the left wrist and 4/5 on flexion of the left small finger. Sensation to pinprick is decreased over the medial aspect of the left ring finger and the palmar and dorsal surfaces of the left small finger; a light tap with a reflex hammer over the cubital tunnel produces paresthesias in these areas. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step in management?
questions.stemHtml: A 42-year-old woman comes to the office because of a 3-month history of a tingling sensation in the ring and small fingers of her left hand. The sensation initially occurred immediately upon awakening each morning and lasted for several minutes. Two months ago, the tingling sensation became more severe and began to awaken her during the night. She also had the onset of similar symptoms in her left arm and elbow during this time. The sensation now occurs throughout the day. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. Vital signs are within normal limits. Muscle strength is 4/5 on abduction and adduction of the left wrist and 4/5 on flexion of the left small finger. Sensation to pinprick is decreased over the medial aspect of the left ring finger and the palmar and dorsal surfaces of the left small finger; a light tap with a reflex hammer over the cubital tunnel produces paresthesias in these areas. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step in management?
choices: Bracing the left elbow in extension during sleep
Surgical decompression of the left cubital tunnel
questions.subject: Neurology

explanationPanel.correct: A. Bracing the left elbow in extension during sleep
explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: Ulnar neuropathy at the level of the elbow may present with

numbness and tingling in the distal ulnar distribution with possible weakness appreciated in distal ulnar-innervated musculature in more severe cases. The most appropriate initial step in management of this patient’s condition is a trial of bracing the left elbow in extension during sleep to limit prolonged flexion.

Evaluation: Ulnar neuropathy most commonly occurs at the level of the elbow or wrist and

may present with sensory deficits or weakness distal to the site of compression or injury.

Definition: Ulnar neuropathy at the level of the elbow, also known as cubital tunnel

syndrome, often presents with numbness and tingling in the fourth and little fingers of the hand. In more severe cases, patients may present with weakness in ulnar-innervated musculature including the first dorsal interosseous, abductor digiti minimi, ulnar portion of the flexor digitorum profundus, and/or flexor carpi ulnaris muscles. Diagnosis may be made clinically and confirmed with electrodiagnostic testing. The examination may include the Tinel sign test at the elbow and prolonged elbow flexion to reproduce the patient’s 12

symptoms.

Prevention: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow may be prevented by avoidance of trauma or

repeated compression of the ulnar nerve either from prolonged elbow flexion or prolonged pressure on the elbows.

Treatment: Treatment begins with conservative measures including activity modification,

bracing of the elbow in extension during sleep, and elbow pads for activities that induce ulnar nerve compression. In refractory cases, surgical decompression and nerve transposition may be considered.

Differential: The patient in this case is presenting with sensory deficits in the fourth and

little finger of the left hand with weakness appreciated in the ulnar-innervated portion of the flexor digitorum profundus. In addition, her symptoms are reproduced with the Tinel sign test at the elbow, which makes ulnar neuropathy at the elbow the most likely diagnosis. Bracing the left elbow in extension during sleep is the most appropriate initial step in management.

wrongAnswers.B: Intramuscular vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin) therapy is not the most appropriate initial step in management. The cause of the patient’s symptoms is likely secondary to ulnar neuropathy at the level of the elbow. Initial management with bracing of the elbow in extension during sleep is more appropriate.
wrongAnswers.C: Oral levetiracetam therapy is incorrect. Levetiracetam often is used in the treatment and prevention of seizures. Conservative management with elbow bracing is more appropriate.
wrongAnswers.D: Oral tramadol therapy is not the most appropriate initial step in management. Although tramadol has been used to address neuropathic pain, it is not the most appropriate initial step in management. The more appropriate initial step would include bracing of the elbow in extension during sleep.
wrongAnswers.E: Surgical decompression of the left cubital tunnel is incorrect. Initial management includes conservative measures such as elbow bracing during sleep or activity modification. If the patient’s symptoms are refractory to conservative management, surgical intervention may be considered.

explanationPanel.rule: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow is initially managed with nighttime elbow extension bracing and activity modification.
explanationPanel.trap: Surgical decompression is reserved for refractory or severe progressive cases, not initial management.

layer4.rule: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow is initially managed with nighttime elbow extension bracing and activity modification.
layer4.trap: Surgical decompression is reserved for refractory or severe progressive cases, not initial management.

Question: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in evaluation?
choices: Serum total IgA and anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA concentrations
Trial of low-fermentable oligo-,di-, and monosaccharides and polyols (FODMAP) diet and use of a symptom diary
questions.subject: Gastroenterology

explanationPanel.correct: D. Serum total IgA and anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA concentrations
explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: This patient with intermittent abdominal bloating, diarrhea,

microcytic anemia, and weight loss most likely has celiac disease. The most appropriate next step in evaluation is to measure serum total IgA and anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA concentrations while the patient is still consuming a diet that contains gluten.

Evaluation: Serum total IgA and anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA concentration

measurement is an important step in the workup for celiac disease. In this young patient with a family history of autoimmune disease, intermittent abdominal bloating and diarrhea, weight loss, and laboratory studies notable for microcytic anemia, celiac disease must be ruled out.

Definition: Celiac disease is an immune-mediated disease triggered by consumption of

gluten. Patients present with symptoms of malabsorption such as diarrhea, weight loss, and vitamin deficiency. The first test often done on these patients is measurement of serum total IgA and anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA concentrations. If the anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA is increased, then esophagogastroduodenoscopy is performed with duodenal biopsy, which is the gold standard for diagnosis.

Prevention: Celiac disease has a genetic predisposition and there are no known

preventions for the disease.

Treatment: The primary treatment for celiac disease is a lifelong gluten-free diet, which

leads to healing of the mucosal lining of the small intestine and symptom resolution.

Differential: The differential diagnosis for this patient is broad and includes diagnoses

such as irritable bowel syndrome, inflammatory bowel disease, and endometriosis.

wrongAnswers.A: CT scan of the abdomen is not indicated in the workup for this patient. CT scan would not provide serologic or histologic diagnosis for celiac disease.
wrongAnswers.B: Gastric emptying study is incorrect. Gastric emptying study is used in the diagnosis of gastroparesis. This patient’s symptoms of malabsorption are more consistent with celiac disease.
wrongAnswers.C: Human leukocyte antigen-B27 haplotype testing is incorrect. Human leukocyte antigen-B27 (HLA-B27) is associated with several diseases, such as ankylosing spondylitis and psoriatic arthritis; it is not associated with celiac disease. HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 are associated with celiac disease.
wrongAnswers.E: Trial of low-fermentable oligo-, di-, and monosaccharides and polyols (FODMAP) diet and use of a symptom diary is incorrect. This refers to the management of suspected irritable bowel syndrome. This patient’s laboratory studies showing microcytic anemia along with the history consistent with celiac disease is an indication to rule out celiac disease prior to treating for irritable bowel syndrome.

explanationPanel.rule: Bloating, chronic diarrhea, weight loss, microcytic anemia, and autoimmune family history require total IgA plus anti-tTG IgA while eating gluten.
explanationPanel.trap: Do not label IBS or start a FODMAP trial before evaluating red flags such as anemia and weight loss.

layer4.rule: Bloating, chronic diarrhea, weight loss, microcytic anemia, and autoimmune family history require total IgA plus anti-tTG IgA while eating gluten.
layer4.trap: Do not label IBS or start a FODMAP trial before evaluating red flags such as anemia and weight loss.

questions.stem: A 79-year-old woman comes to the office for a routine examination. She resides in an assisted living facility. She feels well. She expresses concern about resuming sexual activity with a partner since her husband died 18 years ago. She talks about loneliness, fear of pain with vaginal intercourse, and worry that her children may oppose a new person in their lives. She has hypertension well controlled with lisinopril. She does not use tobacco products, drink alcoholic beverages, or use other substances. She plays tennis twice weekly. She is 162 cm (5 ft 4 in) tall and weighs 71 kg (156 lb); BMI is 27 kg/m². Blood pressure is 136/84 mm Hg. Pelvic examination discloses vulvar skin thinning and no lesions or labial fusion. The physician reassures the patient that she is physically healthy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in addressing this patient's concerns?
questions.stemHtml: A 79-year-old woman comes to the office for a routine examination. She resides in an assisted living facility. She feels well. She expresses concern about resuming sexual activity with a partner since her husband died 18 years ago. She talks about loneliness, fear of pain with vaginal intercourse, and worry that her children may oppose a new person in their lives. She has hypertension well controlled with lisinopril. She does not use tobacco products, drink alcoholic beverages, or use other substances. She plays tennis twice weekly. She is 162 cm (5 ft 4 in) tall and weighs 71 kg (156 lb); BMI is 27 kg/m². Blood pressure is 136/84 mm Hg. Pelvic examination discloses vulvar skin thinning and no lesions or labial fusion. The physician reassures the patient that she is physically healthy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in addressing this patient's concerns?
choices: Ask for clarification about concerns regarding intimacy with a new partner
Reassure the patient that she has nothing to worry about
Recommend a family meeting with the patient's children
questions.subject: Ethics/Social Sciences
questions.topic: Sexual health communication in older adults

explanationPanel.correct: A. Ask for clarification about concerns regarding intimacy with a new partner
explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: The most appropriate next step is to ask for clarification

about this patient’s concerns regarding intimacy with a new partner. Having a better understanding of her concerns will help facilitate a conversation to better address her underlying worries.

Evaluation: This patient is a healthy older adult expressing concerns about resuming

sexual activity, including emotional and physical worries. A thorough evaluation should include a sensitive, open-ended discussion to explore her feelings about intimacy, potential fears, and social pressures.

Definition: This patient is experiencing sexual health concerns related to aging, including

genitourinary syndrome of menopause, previously known as vaginal atrophy, as well as psychosocial anxiety about intimacy. Genitourinary syndrome of menopause may present with physical symptoms such as vulvovaginal dryness, dyspareunia, decreased arousal, and possible urinary tract syndromes.

Prevention: While aging-related sexual health changes cannot be entirely prevented,

regular communication about emotional well-being and healthy sexual aging can promote resilience. Early discussions about menopause and postmenopausal sexual changes may decrease anxiety and stigma.

Treatment: Initial treatment includes empathetic dialogue to clarify the patient’s concerns

about intimacy and provide reassurance. If physical symptoms such as vaginal dryness are prominent, vaginal estrogen or lubricants may be appropriate.

Differential: This patient has physical examination findings of vulvar skin thinning with no

lesions or labial fusion. Her concerns regarding intimacy with a new partner should be explored with an open-ended discussion to further address her underlying worries.

wrongAnswers.B: Prescribe estradiol cream is incorrect. A prescription of estradiol cream may be appropriate for patients who have already trialed vaginal moisturizers and lubricants. Further exploring this patient’s concerns regarding intimacy with a new partner is the more appropriate next step.
wrongAnswers.C: Reassure the patient that she has nothing to worry about is not the most appropriate next step. Reassuring this patient without further exploring her concerns would be dismissive and limit the ability to address underlying concerns. Asking for clarification about concerns regarding intimacy is more appropriate.
wrongAnswers.D: Recommend a family meeting with the patient's children is incorrect. Asking for further clarification regarding her concerns is more appropriate. If this patient’s primary underlying concern is fear of her children opposing a new person in their lives, then a family meeting may be appropriate.
wrongAnswers.E: Recommend using a vaginal lubricant is not the most appropriate next step. The use of a vaginal lubricant is often the first-line therapy for patients with genitourinary syndrome of menopause. However, further exploring this patient’s concerns is more appropriate.

explanationPanel.rule: When an older adult raises intimacy concerns, first clarify the patient’s specific worries with open-ended discussion.
explanationPanel.trap: Jumping straight to lubricant or estrogen ignores psychosocial concerns and may miss what the patient is actually asking.

layer4.rule: When an older adult raises intimacy concerns, first clarify the patient’s specific worries with open-ended discussion.
layer4.trap: Jumping straight to lubricant or estrogen ignores psychosocial concerns and may miss what the patient is actually asking.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man is admitted to the intensive care unit following operative repair of injuries he sustained in a motor vehicle collision. The patient underwent a splenectomy, partial hepatectomy, and open fixation of a complex left tibial fracture. The morning after the operation, the patient reports severe pain in his left lower extremity; the pain is more severe than his abdominal postoperative pain. Neurologic examination shows weakness of left foot dorsiflexion and loss of sensation between the left great and second toes. Prompt treatment is necessary to prevent which of the following complications in this patient?
questions.stemHtml: A 22-year-old man is admitted to the intensive care unit following operative repair of injuries he sustained in a motor vehicle collision. The patient underwent a splenectomy, partial hepatectomy, and open fixation of a complex left tibial fracture. The morning after the operation, the patient reports severe pain in his left lower extremity; the pain is more severe than his abdominal postoperative pain. Neurologic examination shows weakness of left foot dorsiflexion and loss of sensation between the left great and second toes. Prompt treatment is necessary to prevent which of the following complications in this patient?
questions.subject: Musculoskeletal/Orthopedics

explanationPanel.whyCorrect:
Educational Objective: Tibial fractures present a high risk for the development of

compartment syndrome, which is most likely the cause of this patient’s symptoms. Compromised blood supply in cases of compartment syndrome may cause tissue ischemia and necrosis leading to rhabdomyolysis.

Evaluation: Signs and symptoms of compartment syndrome include pain out of proportion

to examination findings, pain with passive movement of the muscles, paresthesia, pallor, pulselessness, and paralysis.

Definition: Compartment syndrome may develop in cases of tibial fracture due to blood

vessel injury, muscle injury, inflammation, and edema leading to increased pressure in a compartment of the lower leg. Compromised blood supply deprives muscle and tissue of oxygen and glucose, leading to tissue ischemia and necrosis. Muscle necrosis leads to rhabdomyolysis, myoglobinuria, and possible acute kidney injury.

Prevention: Compartment syndrome may be prevented with the avoidance of trauma.

Treatment: Compartment syndrome is treated by immediate fasciotomy. Fasciotomy

decreases compartment pressure and supports tissue perfusion.

Differential: This patient with a complex left tibial fracture is experiencing severe pain,

weakness, and loss of sensation postoperatively. Compartment syndrome is the most likely cause of his symptoms, which can lead to the development of rhabdomyolysis.

wrongAnswers.A: Acute respiratory distress syndrome is incorrect. Acute respiratory distress syndrome may occur in response to severe trauma, including burns. Acute respiratory distress syndrome results from cytokine-mediated injury to the pulmonary parenchyma, especially the alveolar epithelium and endothelium, resulting in diffuse alveolar damage with consequent exudative fluid filling the alveolar spaces. This patient presents with signs and symptoms of compartment syndrome, which may lead to the development of rhabdomyolysis.
wrongAnswers.B: Clostridium difficile colitis is not a likely complication. C. difficile colitis is an opportunistic infection that most commonly occurs after the use of antibiotics. The condition typically presents with abdominal pain and severe watery diarrhea.
wrongAnswers.C: Disseminated intravascular coagulation is incorrect. Disseminated intravascular coagulation is a systemic disorder that can be provoked by trauma, sepsis, malignancy, pancreatitis, toxins, and multiple other causes. Endothelial dysfunction leads to overwhelming activation of the clotting cascade, resulting in microthrombi formation and depletion of platelets and clotting factors. Rhabdomyolysis is a more likely complication of compartment syndrome.
wrongAnswers.E: Systemic sepsis is not the most likely complication to develop. Fever, tachycardia, and hypotension in the postoperative period should raise suspicion for sepsis. This patient presents with signs and symptoms of compartment syndrome, which may lead to the development of rhabdomyolysis.

explanationPanel.rule: Compartment syndrome after tibial fracture causes ischemic muscle necrosis that can progress to rhabdomyolysis.
explanationPanel.trap: Do not be distracted by generic postoperative complications when pain out of proportion plus neurologic deficits localize to compartment syndrome.

layer4.rule: Compartment syndrome after tibial fracture causes ischemic muscle necrosis that can progress to rhabdomyolysis.
layer4.trap: Do not be distracted by generic postoperative complications when pain out of proportion plus neurologic deficits localize to compartment syndrome.
